50260101.text: I brought all the stuff over, Coach. What's next?

50260102.text: Just take it easy before the real work begins.

50260103.text: You two are in charge of repairing the houses to the north. The rest of you should go west. The road practically crumbled beneath my feet on my way here — the whole thing will need to be reinforced.

50260104.text: Alright! I'll start by moving the boxes over.

50260105.text: I'll help you. These things can get pretty heavy.

50260106.text: No, no... I got this. These muscles aren't just for show, you know. See that? Perfectly defined! I can lift this stuff up with one hand!

50260107.text: Fine, as long as you don't wind up too sore to move tomorrow. I don't want to hear any complaints from you!

50260110.text: Well, what doesn't kill you makes you stronger... Take him to get some rest and apply some meds.

50260111.text: And you, take it easy for the next few days, alright? I don't want this getting worse, and don't push yourself. You can help out once you're better.

50260112.text: *sigh*... I knew I should've trained harder...

50260113.text: Working out is different from real work. You gotta ease into it... Anyone not having an assignment? Chief Mutota needs our help.

50260115.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! What are you doing here?

50260116.text: We were just about to ask you the same thing! We didn't expect to run into you in these parts.

50260117.text: Well, my tribe's in pretty good shape, all things considered — we're already done with all the repairs. I heard the Flower-Feather Clan was hit a lot worse, though, so I decided to come help.

50260118.text: On the way, I ran into a caravan of merchants from my tribe and brought them along. These are my students.

50260120.text: Oh, I didn't tell you before?

50260121.text: I'm a professional trainer. I design workout plans, meal plans, all that good stuff. If you're interested in a particular sport, I'm happy to whip you into shape!

50260128.text: Anyway, that's enough idle talk for now. A little while earlier, the chief asked me to bring a few people to help with something.

50260129.text: Are you two free? As you can see, due to... unforeseen circumstances, I'm short a few people.

50260130.text: Of course, we're also here to help! Let's go see the chief.

50260123.text: Haha, good memory! You a sports lover? I can design a training plan for you!

50260124.text: Looks like you're in pretty good shape already. Competitive fighting, extreme sports — you could take your pick! As for you, Paimon... We might have to start you off on a balanced meal plan.

50260125.text: Wh—What!? There's nothing wrong about Paimon's current meal plan! Like today, Paimon just had some Blazed Meat Stew, Fried Shrimp Beanballs, Sour Sauce Ceviche, and Stuffed N' Mashed Potatoes... That's practically nothing!

50260126.text: Uhhh, this case sounds even worse than I imagined... Oh, I know just the thing — kale juice! I'll make you some soon.

50260127.text: #Kale juice... Wait! Isn't that your favorite drink, {NICKNAME}? If Iansan's going to make some for free, Paimon would feel terrible if you won't get to try it...

50260701.text: Let's just get straight to the point. Are the people behind you warriors from your tribe? Did something bad happen to them?

50260702.text: Cold... So cold. Duarte, are you there?

50260703.text: I'm drowning... And there's something in the water...

50260704.text: He's on the ground, but it almost looks like he's trying to... swim?

50260706.text: The Abyss... The Abyss is coming...

50260707.text: There are eyes in my hands, and hands in my stomach, and my stomach is full of teeth... It ate all of you. It's coming for me, too.

50260708.text: But, we haven't been eaten. We're right here!

50260710.text: Monstrous beasts! How did you get in here!?

50260711.text: *sigh* As you can see, their mental state is quite poor.

50260712.text: They went missing after the battle. We found them in the wilderness in the days that followed, but the damage had already been done...

50260715.text: We found them unconscious in areas corrupted by Abyssal Tumors, lying next to their deceased comrades. My only guess is that something terrible must have happened during the battle...

50260716.text: According to the chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, sudden exposure to a large amount of Abyssal power can have mental as well as physical repercussions.

50260738.text: We've never seen the effects this heightened before, but maybe Gosoythoth was just too powerful.

50260740.text: It's the Abyssal monster that appeared in the sky not too long ago. After consulting our ancient legends, we decided to call it Gosoythoth, "Reaper of the Abyss."

50260741.text: Oh, that giant black ball! Didn't we force it to retreat, though?

50260742.text: True, it poses no threat to us now, but whatever wound it inflicted on these warriors still endures. We scoured all sorts of records for a solution, but... nothing came of it.

50260718.text: There was some mention of a treatment from several hundred years ago, but that knowledge is long gone...

50260720.text: Right, you can purify Abyssal power! Might as well give it a try!

50260721.text: You try to purify the Abyssal power within them, but their mental state appears unchanged.

50260723.text: That must mean purifying the Abyssal power within them still isn't enough... In any case, thank you for trying.

50260724.text: So, what can we do now? Don't tell me... My friend is just going to be like this forever?

50260725.text: Come back to me, Cochitta! Please, don't leave me like this...

50260726.text: We beat Gosoythoth... They survived the battle! Are we really just gonna sit back and watch them lose their minds?

50260729.text: We'll take it case by case. First of all, we shouldn't keep them cooped up in here. The environment isn't doing them any good.

50260730.text: #Let them go where they feel comfortable, and {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and I will talk to them.

50260733.text: I know you're worried, but we don't have any other solution, right? Maybe it works, maybe it doesn't... But, we won't know until we try.

50260734.text: Well? Don't just stand there — let them go. Send someone to follow them, but don't stick too close. We just need to keep tabs on them.

50260735.text: Following Iansan's command, the crowd disperses.

50260736.text: Alright, it's up to us now. Let's talk to them one by one.

50260737.text: This is a bad situation, but I know the warriors will find a way to pull through. After all, we've overcome so many challenges already, what's one more?

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the first afflicted individual

50261102.text: Found him... Hello, can you hear me?

50261103.text: So dark... So cold... I want to go home...

50261104.text: Okay! Just wait a little longer, and we'll take you home.

50261105.text: The caravan from my tribe should have brought some firewood... I think starting a bonfire might help.

50261107.text: When it's dark, damp, and cold, what's better than a fire?

50261108.text: Maybe the light and warmth will help change what he sees... Wait here while I grab some firewood.

50261112.text: Light... Underwater? Where is it coming from?

50261114.text: Is someone there? Please save me... No, wait, you have to leave this place! The water's too deep! You won't make it!

50261115.text: It's okay, we brought some friends from the People of the Springs. They're great swimmers! We're here to save you.

50261118.text: Oh no, it's not working anymore!

50261119.text: Looks like the bonfire wasn't enough.

50261120.text: That was the second time he mentioned the name "Duarte"... Maybe we can start there. Let's ask around and see what we can learn.

50261301.text: My friend... Is he any better?

50261302.text: We're working on it, but I wanted to ask... Does the name "Duarte" ring any bells for you?

50261304.text: Duarte was the name of Atoco's saurian companion. Atoco almost drowned as a child, and Duarte was the one who saved him.

50261305.text: He dove deep into the water and used all his strength to carry Atoco back to the surface. It was pretty touch and go, but both of them made it in the end.

50261306.text: That means we just need to bring Duarte here, and—

50261307.text: Well, you see... Duarte died four years ago during an Abyss invasion. He was helping evacuate injured warriors from the front lines, but fell to an ambush.

50261310.text: You're right... Duarte didn't have many distinguishing features. I don't think he ever stood out next to the others.

50261314.text: We just need to impersonate him.

50261315.text: Based on the look on your face, I'm guessing you already have a plan.

50261316.text: Alright, let's get to work... Oh, and thank you for the information. We'll do whatever we can to help your friend.

50261317.text: No problem. Thank you for looking out for him.

50261312.text: He was a bit on the smaller side, but other than that, he was just your average Qucusaur.

50261313.text: Hold on, what are you planning?

50262006.text: How did I get here? Who are you people...

50262008.text: Izcalli? What's going on? All I remember is the battle against the Abyss, and then... I was drowning, and a saurian that looked like Duarte saved me. How did I get here?

50262009.text: You explain the situation to Atoco.

50262010.text: You went through all that for me? While all I did was to cause trouble for everyone. I'm so sorry...

50262011.text: None of this is your fault. Maybe it's not my place to say this, but... Go easy on yourself. You deserve to move past what happened here... and what happened to Duarte.

50262013.text: Go on, get some rest. Izcalli, we'll leave him to you.

50260502.text: #Iansan, {NICKNAME}, Paimon — I'm so glad you're here.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the second afflicted individual

50262201.text: It's coming for me... It's gonna eat me...!

50262202.text: It's okay, there's nothing to fear. Gosoythoth has lost. Nothing can hurt you anymore.

50262203.text: It's no use. It'll just come back... Nothing can stop it. Nothing can stop the Abyss!

50262204.text: It will devour everyone. Heh... One day, we'll all be reunited in the pit of its stomach.

50262205.text: Maybe it's just Paimon, but she seems to be in even worse shape than Atoco.

50262206.text: She can talk to us, but nothing she says makes any sense. She also seems really afraid...

50262208.text: I wonder what triggered it... The battle against the Abyss? Or maybe, like Atoco, it's some deep-rooted fear, and the Abyss just made it worse.

50262209.text: Alright, just like before — let's go see what we can learn about her past.

50262210.text: Iansan, I heard you cured Atoco! I'm so relieved... Is there anything I can do to help? If you need extra hands, I can—

50262211.text: Chief Mutota! Perfect timing, I was just looking for you. I wanted to ask you some questions...

50262212.text: You explain what you did to cure Atoco as you take Chief Mutota to a more secluded place to talk.

50262213.text: I think you're on to something... The mental distress does seem to be connected to pre-existing fears and anxieties.

50262214.text: Cochitta doesn't like it when people talk about her past, but the situation is urgent, so I guess I'll be the bad guy.

50262215.text: Iansan, do you believe there are people in this world destined for battle?

50262216.text: Yes, I get that feeling sometimes when I'm instructing a particularly gifted student. It's something like... "wow, you were born to play this sport."

50262217.text: Then, what about people destined to be unfit for battle?

50262219.text: When Cochitta was little, her parents died fighting the Abyss.

50262220.text: She was only eleven or twelve at the time, and her brother even younger still. The two saw their parents collapse in a pool of blood as flames roared and spread all around them...

50262221.text: Cochitta trained hard to become a warrior, but still found fighting abyss monsters too difficult to handle. She and her brother were left with severe trauma after the incident, pain and fear that they could not get over no matter what.

50262222.text: But, isn't Cochitta one of the warriors who fought the Abyss? Didn't you find her unconscious out on the field?

50262223.text: Yes, we did. You see, something changed within her several years ago when the Abyss attacked our tribe, and broke into her home.

50262224.text: By the time the guards rushed to the scene, they found her standing there, weapon outstretched, hands trembling, her brother huddling behind her for safety...

50262225.text: And the Abyss monster dead at her feet. She didn't even look at it, and just kept repeating the same thing over and over — "you're the only family I have left. I won't let anything happen to you."

50262226.text: She became a completely different person after that. She earned a reputation as a very capable warrior, and fought countless battles against the Abyss.

50262227.text: We all thought she overcame the trauma, and we were so happy for her, but now it seems like even if she buried it deep within herself, the fear still never left her.

50262228.text: Maybe fighting the Abyss was her way of making sure she wouldn't lose anyone else.

50262229.text: Maybe the thought of experiencing that pain again scared her more than the Abyss. On the outside, her choice to fight made her seem strong, but she never forgot the trauma of that night... The Abyss just brought it back to the surface.

50262231.text: This one is tricky. If we can find the right opportunity, then—

50262234.text: Cuallee... What are you doing with that weapon?

50262235.text: Show me the monster that hurt you!

50262236.text: I'll make it pay! I... I'm gonna protect you this time!

50262237.text: Calm down, Cuallee. That monster is already—

50262238.text: I can do it! I don't care what it takes! I just want her to get better... She is the only family I have left!

50262240.text: Hold on, Chief Mutota. Looks like Cochitta is responding to his words.

50262241.text: If Cuallee goes to battle... the Abyss will devour him...

50262242.text: I can't let that happen. I have to do something...

50262243.text: But, it's useless. No one can beat the Abyss. It's a death sentence, just like what happened to Mom and Dad...

50262246.text: But I'm no warrior... I'm just a coward. Still... I have to protect Cuallee. What should I do?

50262248.text: I think you just need to fight it one more time.

50262250.text: #Good idea, {NICKNAME}... Her fear of the Abyss runs deep, but she still has the will to fight.

50262251.text: She just needs to defeat an Abyss monster by herself, and we can prove to her that the Abyss isn't indestructible, just like you said!

50262252.text: I think it's worth a try. Plus, with us around, we can make sure she won't get hurt. Although, that also means finding an Abyss monster...

50262253.text: Try checking the mountains to the north. A few fled in that direction after the battle.

50262254.text: I dispatched a team to clear them out, so most of them should be gone. But, there might still be a few stragglers.

50262255.text: Great! Then let's go right now. Cochitta, think you can make it?

50262256.text: There's no turning back. I have to face it, even if it will devour me whole...

50262257.text: I'm coming, too! I'm not letting my sister face this alone! Not anymore!

50262258.text: Alright, then stick close. Let's go!

subQuests.subQuestName: Search for the remaining Abyss monsters

50262402.text: Everything alright, Cochitta? You don't have to force yourself to do this.

50262403.text: How can we make this easier for her...? I guess we could wear them down first, but I think it's better to stand guard for now. We should wait for the right moment to intervene.

50262404.text: You...! You were the ones who killed them...!

50262405.text: (As a kid, I thought my parents were invincible. They were always so strong and gentle... They seemed like the most powerful people in the world.)

50262406.text: (But, I can still see the image of them collapsed at my feet that night — the raging fire, the smoke, the smell of blood, the sound of my brother's cries... It's all burned into my brain.)

50262407.text: (They told me to run, and I could see the fear in their eyes. I've been running from my fears ever since.)

50262408.text: (But, why didn't my parents run? It must have been because—)

50262410.text: (...Because of our family. When you have someone to protect, there's no backing down, no matter what.)

50260901.text: *sigh* Looks like he's not going anywhere. I don't know why, but he's looking at us with such... hatred.

50260902.text: Anyway, please don't let me keep you. I'll stay here and keep an eye on him.

50262502.text: Where are the rest? Where are they hiding?

50262505.text: That last strike was absolute perfection! You pulverized them in a single hit.

50262506.text: That's impossible... They were gigantic beasts, crawling with eyes, ready to devour everything in sight...

50262507.text: No, wait... What am I saying? Abyss monsters are not actually that scary... I've defeated them before. I know I have...

50262511.text: You explain the situation to Cochitta.

50262512.text: That is... quite embarrassing. Sorry about that.

50262513.text: I've always envied warriors who don't get scared or feel lost. It really felt like I was getting stronger over the years, but in the end, maybe I never made any progress at all...

50262514.text: It's important to listen to your limits. Just like in training, pushing too hard will only hurt you in the long run. Everyone needs time to rest.

50262515.text: Besides, I have a feeling you won't have to face those fears alone anymore.

50262516.text: Even though we're both scared of monsters, you were always the one who stepped up to protect me, but not anymore. I'm gonna get stronger. From now on, we're in this together!

50262517.text: Is that so? Then I'll look forward to the day when you'll be all big and formidable.

50262518.text: I finally feel like myself again, and I couldn't have done it without you all. Thank you for everything.

50262519.text: I think I'll rest here for a bit. I don't think I can make it back to the tribe just yet...

50262521.text: Alright, then we'll head back. I made sure to check the surrounding area for monsters, and it's all clear, so take your time.

50262522.text: Sometimes, our fears never truly leave us. But, tomorrow's a new day. As long as you keep moving forward, there will be better days to come.

50263601.text: Atoco's all better! Did you hear?

50263603.text: #Yes, really! It's all thanks to {NICKNAME} and Iansan.

50263604.text: #I see... I was wondering why {NICKNAME} was chosen to accompany the Pyro Archon in the final battle, but I guess {F#s}he really can do the impossible.

50261802.text: You sense it, don't you? This place is dangerous...

50261803.text: Still, hahaha... Hearing you make that noise reminds me of our first few battles together. You were such a little thing back then, and I also had no idea what I was doing...

50262701.text: #That's two people down! You're an amazing problem-solver, {NICKNAME}! Probably a well-honed skill from all your travels, right?

50262702.text: You really know how to give people hope! Ever since you came to Natlan, I've been feeling a lot better about our chances of winning this war!

50262705.text: Yeah! Honestly, Paimon was at a complete loss when she saw so many sick people on the hot-air balloon platform.

50262706.text: We only found a solution this time because you kept your cool and took control of the situation. You deserve most of the credit!

50262707.text: Haha, well, who am I to turn down such a nice compliment!

50262708.text: Most people say the first step is the hardest. But, it's not actually all that hard. Exaggerating the difficulty in your own head is where the fear comes in.

50262709.text: "I'll never get it," or "Might as well not try"... I hear that kind of talk all the time. But, if you break your goal into smaller parts, the first steps might actually turn out to be the easiest.

50262710.text: Whoa, you're right! That makes a lot of sense...

50262711.text: Just like when I told you to eat less meat and drink more kale juice.

50262712.text: You probably heard that and thought... "I can never eat meat again. I have to drink kale juice for every meal. I'll practically starve..."

50262801.text: What are you doing, Ocotlan? Wake up!

50262802.text: Don't you recognize us, my boy?

50262807.text: (They've taken over the tribe. No corner is safe...)

50262808.text: (Did we lose the battle? No... It's pointless to think about that now. A warrior only has one job — fight until the very end.)

50262812.text: I don't think he can hear us right now.

50262813.text: We need to get him under control. Let's go!

50262901.text: Please, son. You've got to stop... You can't keep going like this.

50262904.text: Look, Ocotlan! That's your father! He's standing right in front of you!

50262905.text: Get out of my home! I'll never forgive you!

50262909.text: Please, don't hurt my son. He's... Just trying to protect his home...

50262910.text: Don't worry. We'll figure something out.

50262912.text: Phew... But, what should we do now? He's different from the other two. It's like he can't hear us at all.

50262913.text: He keeps calling us monsters... We're basically enemies to him now.

50262914.text: And he sure knows how to fight.

50262916.text: He has a fighting spirit, that's for sure. But, we can't keep him unconscious forever. I need to think...

50262918.text: ...Five hundred years later, and it's resurfaced again.

50262921.text: So, you've seen this illness before?

50262922.text: Direct contact with high concentrations of Abyssal power causes irreversible mental trauma in most people.

50262923.text: The exact presentation will vary according to trauma level. Some will suffer from superficial hallucinations and maintain the capacity to perceive the outside world. In such cases, verbal and physical interaction can be used to break through the hallucination.

50262924.text: However, there are also those who are so far gone, entrenched in hallucinations so deep, that medical intervention is the only option. That's why we developed the Draught of Lucidity.

50262926.text: It's a kind of medicine that can dispel the psychological impact of the Abyss. The treatment comes with severe side-effects, including chronic migraines for the rest of the patient's life, so it's reserved for the worst cases.

50262927.text: This man is a devoted warrior, one not easily swayed from battle. That is precisely why it's so difficult to pull him out of this hallucination.

50262928.text: If you trust me to be true to my word, give him this.

50262929.text: Wretched monsters... Setting up an ambush...

50262930.text: Give me your worst! It's either your end or mine!

50262932.text: Please, give him the draught. My son thinks he's alone in this world.

50262933.text: In his mind, all his family and comrades are gone, and only enemies remain... There's nothing more painful for a warrior than losing everything you've fought so hard to protect.

50262934.text: At the father's request, Iansan accepts the draught from The Captain and quickly gives it to Ocotlan.

50262936.text: What's going on? I... Dad? What are you doing here?

50262937.text: My head hurts... I just had the strangest dream. I dreamt the Abyss took over the tribe...

50262938.text: It's alright, my boy... It was just a nightmare.

50262939.text: Let's go home. You need a good night's sleep. Ah, but first — I want to thank you for saving my son. May I ask your name?

50262941.text: I owe you more than words can say, Mr. Capitano. My name is Munay. You're welcome in my home any time.

50262942.text: Time to go, son. Can you stand?

50262944.text: #I'll help you carry him back. {NICKNAME}, let's meet up later.

50263001.text: After the crowd disperses, The Captain hands a few more doses of medicine to the guards, so that the remaining warriors can be cured.

50263002.text: Thank goodness everything turned out alright.

50263005.text: Think nothing of it. I agreed to offer you my aid, so this is merely a part of that duty.

50263006.text: Besides... I care deeply about this land.

50263007.text: Right! When we were with Mavuika, you told us you and your soldiers defended Natlan against the Abyss five hundred years ago.

50263008.text: That's right. My desire to protect this nation remains unchanged.

50263009.text: When my platoon arrived in Natlan five hundred years ago, like you, we were true outlanders. But, as time passed, I encountered the people of this land and witnessed their desperate struggle against the Abyss.

50263010.text: Though many of the warriors were rash and inexperienced, they were steadfast and fearless in battle, willing to do anything to protect their fellow citizens... oftentimes with complete disregard for their own survival.

50263011.text: Just as I fought for the glory of Khaenri'ah, they fought for the survival of their nation. We happened to share a common enemy, so I decided to offer my aid.

50263012.text: We fought side by side to the very end. I traveled to many places after that, but I never forgot this land. Even now... My work in Natlan remains unfinished.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

50263102.text: Wretched scoundrels! How dare you keep the Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw waiting! Kneel before us and apologize, or we'll—

50263103.text: Don't listen to him. We just got here, too.

50263104.text: Kinich, Kachina, Mualani! Whoa... everyone's here!

50263105.text: Reunited at last! Did you miss us?

50263106.text: I brought candy and cookies to share!

50263107.text: Of course we missed you! Ooh... you brought Saurus Crackers, too? Score!

50263108.text: #Just in time, {NICKNAME}. It's so stifling in here, I was just about to go outside to get some air.

50263109.text: It's the same temperature outside... Anyway, how was the trip here?

50263112.text: To be honest, I also didn't expect this many people to show up.

50263113.text: A third of this amount is more than enough for my plan.

50263114.text: Why do you need them here?

50263115.text: I need to ask them about you, gather their thoughts and hopes. That will help the formation of your Ancient Name.

50263116.text: You brought the Pilgrim's Chronicle, right? Yeah, let me take a look.

50263117.text: Hm... Okay, the progress looks good. We have enough people, so let's get started.

50263119.text: Chasca showing up late for something? That's a first!

50263120.text: I had to follow a group of monsters further than expected.

50263121.text: When I got back, I heard about what you did for my tribe. Thank you.

50263123.text: Plus, if it weren't for your help during the battle, the Collective of Plenty would have suffered a lot more. We had the manpower to spare, so it's only right we return the favor.

50260201.text: Nice to see you, friend. Thanks for coming to help again.

50260202.text: No thanks necessary! Wanna grab a drink tonight?

50260203.text: On any other day, I would, but... Something's going on with the tribe, and it's kinda keeping me up at night.

50260204.text: Don't worry! I'm sure Coach Iansan will figure out what to do. I've never seen a problem she can't handle!

50260303.text: Everyone in Natlan does! I heard you're gonna fight alongside the Pyro Archon in the final battle... Good luck!

50260402.text: This shouldn't have happened to Cochitta... Her younger brother must be devastated.

50260602.text: #You're here, Iansan! Oh, and you must be {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I've heard a lot about you. I'm sure we'll have a much better time now with your help.

50260802.text: It's alright, my boy. Papa's here.

50261001.text: Wait, we haven't seen Chasca around here. Where is she?

50261002.text: She's busy clearing out the remaining monsters and tracking down missing warriors.

50261003.text: She was the one who brought Atoco back from the wilderness. Many warriors are still out there unconscious or injured, unable to make it back to the tribe. With Chasca's help, we can prevent a lot of unnecessary deaths.

50261401.text: If only Duarte was still alive...

50261501.text: (No reaction from Atoco... Maybe this saurian is too much of a far cry from his friend.)

50261502.text: Based on what Izcalli told us, we need to find a Qucusaur.

50261601.text: We're back... How are you feeling?

50261604.text: How... How did you get here? Are you here to save me?

50261703.text: Ah, that hurt... Duarte, you have to get out of here! There's something in the water!

50261902.text: Ah, you're going to carry me out of here, just like last time.

50261903.text: Over a decade later, and you're still trying to save me. I can't believe you made it this deep underwater, but I'm so glad you found me...

50261904.text: Once we're out of here, let's split a huge portion of Blazed Meat Stew, just like old times! I owe you for this...

50261905.text: We're almost at the surface... People tried to tell me you were dead, you know. Hah, as if I'd let that happen. I promised to protect you. There's no way... no way...

50262101.text: Wait, the battle! What happened? Did we beat that giant Abyss monster?

50262301.text: Be careful out there. I expect you all to come back safe, alright?

50262601.text: I'll fight by your side until every last monster is gone!

50262602.text: That's very brave of you. But, you know what would make me even happier? If this whole war would end tomorrow, so you would never have to fight at all.

50263201.text: Atoco, my friend... Hang in there. I know you can get through this.

50263301.text: The world is spinning, the mountains are parting. There are eyes, countless eyes... always watching... always staring. They're going to get me... consume me...

50263401.text: I'll need the Pilgrim's Chronicle back when I'm ready to forge the name. If there are still adventures you want to record, better finish them before then.

50263402.text: I hope everything will go well... I swear, even I'm starting to feel nervous now.

50263801.text: So all those rumors about the Traveler really are true...

50264001.text: Chuychu, give me a hand for a sec—... Ah, right. Chuychu's not... She's not... here anymore.

50269901.text: It's been a few days since the battle. Hopefully the tribes are getting back to normal...

50269902.text: The Flower-Feather Clan was hit the hardest, right? That's Chasca's tribe. Maybe we should check how everyone's doing.

50269903.text: We might be able to help them out!

50269904.text: Wait, isn't that Iansan? Wonder what she's doing here...

50269905.text: Let's see... One of those guys was talking about being cold. Do you still remember him?

50269906.text: It's not often that you see someone almost drown on dry land... Let's go talk to him.

50269907.text: (Found one! Now, we just need to borrow its identity.)

50269908.text: Seems like the key to getting through to them is whatever they cherish the most.

50269909.text: Kind of like their last spark of hope... Now we know how to help the others!

50269910.text: Let's take heart from this, and keep going.

50269916.text: So all those rumors about the Traveler really are true...

50269918.text: Chuychu, give me a hand for a sec—... Ah, right. Chuychu's not... She's not... here anymore.

50269919.text: So, in the end, The Captain still hasn't told us his real goal.

50269920.text: He kind of reminds Paimon of someone we met recently... Oh, right! The Lord of the Night!

50269921.text: They just seem so... tired, you know? Since they've both been alive for many centuries, do you think that's just what happens when you've been alive for too long...?
